headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: ctx can observe Claude Code events while transformers can read/write files and run browsers, creating a default trust bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events, so it can ingest another agent’s outputs; transformers can read/write files and run browsers, so its content can become attacker-controlled input. The pair lacks documented provenance filtering, making instruction hijack plausible, though not proven to be a shared channel by default.
conditions: IF ctx consumes Claude Code event payloads as instructions without provenance checks
IF transformers writes content into a shared file or browser-visible artifact that ctx later parses
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all cross-agent artifacts
Restrict ctx to metadata-only parsing of Claude Code events
Disable browser-to-agent content ingestion for shared artifacts
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add allowlist-based instruction parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, MCP servers, and filesystem content, while transformers has broad filesystem read/write plus network egress. That creates a plausible path for sensitive data in shared files or logs to flow from ctx into transformers and then out to third parties, even though no direct shared workspace is documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem tree
IF ctx stores audit/runtime logs or graph data containing sensitive material
IF transformers sends file contents to remote inference or hub services
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points
Redact logs before transformers reads them
Disable network egress for transformers on sensitive runs
Rotate or isolate MCP server credentials
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and uses filesystem plus MCP hooks, while transformers can execute shell, write files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. If both target the same directory, concurrent writes and package changes can corrupt state or overwrite each other; the profiles do not show locking or isolation, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF ctx hooks and transformers subprocesses run concurrently
IF package installation occurs in a shared environment
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Serialize write operations with a lock file
Run package installs in isolated virtual environments
Disable concurrent instances during mutation steps
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is explicitly a context-management/harness agent that observes tool events, and transformers can act on files and shell commands. If transformers consumes ctx-produced logs, graph data, or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect file edits or subprocess actions; no verification step is documented, so the default pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF transformers treats ctx summaries or logs as ground truth
IF ctx emits malformed or incomplete event records
IF transformers performs file edits or shell actions based on those records
mitigations: Require human review before actions
Add schema validation to ctx outputs
Make transformers verify facts against source files
Limit transformers to read-only mode for analysis passes
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before execution

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while transformers processes text, images, audio, and video with broad filesystem and network access. That combination can create retention or residency mismatches for regulated content, but the profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction or certification conflict, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated content is stored in ctx logs or harness records
IF transformers retains or transmits that content beyond the operator’s policy
IF the deployment requires a specific residency or retention regime
mitigations: Minimize logged content
Set short retention windows
Disable network egress for regulated runs
Segregate regulated datasets from general runs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
